name: Rocket Money
tagline: Finds the recurring charges on your bank feed, cancels the ones you forgot, budgets the rest

pricing.plan: Premium (pay what you think is fair)
pricing.notes: Official page checked 2026-07-30: Premium is pay-what-you-think-is-fair, typically 7 to 14 USD per month after a 7-day trial, and priceMonthly uses the 7 USD floor. Bill negotiation is priced separately and is open to free accounts too: 35 to 60 percent of the first year's savings, charged only when it works.

verdictSummary: Plaid hands you the only hard part and it turns out not to be hard: link accounts in the browser, sync transactions nightly, and recurrence is a group-by with a date-gap check. One session gets a working subscription radar, price-hike alerts, budgets, and a net worth chart, on your own machine, with the free tier of Plaid covering a personal number of banks. What one session does not get is the person at Rocket Money who emails Sirius XM on your behalf. That concierge, and the phone in your pocket that buzzes when a balance drops, is what Premium actually sells.
coreLoopDIY: Link accounts through Plaid, sync transactions nightly, cluster them into recurring merchants with a cadence and a predicted next charge, and render subscriptions, budgets, and net worth on one local dashboard.
requirements: Plaid developer account (free sandbox, self-serve production)
Resend or SMTP for the weekly digest
a cron tick that actually runs
whatYouLose: the team that cancels a subscription on your behalf
bill negotiation, which is people on the phone, not code
the iOS and Android apps with balance and charge alerts
credit score and full credit report monitoring
Rocket's merchant database, which names the charge you cannot recognize
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because spotting the charge is the easy half. The half people actually want is somebody else doing the cancelling and the haggling, and a phone that tells them before the money leaves.

notes: The detection is a group-by. The cancellation is a person. Plaid gives away the only part that looks hard.
prompt:
Build me a local subscription radar and budget dashboard to replace Rocket Money.
Requirements:

- Node 22 + Express + better-sqlite3, server-rendered EJS with a little vanilla JS
  and Chart.js. No frontend framework, no build step, binds to 127.0.0.1 only.
- Bank data comes from Plaid: Link in the browser, one access_token per Item in
  SQLite, and a nightly node-cron tick calling /transactions/sync with the cursor
  persisted so every run is incremental. Keys in .env, sandbox until I flip one var.
- Recurring detection is the whole point: group by normalized merchant and rounded
  amount, call it recurring at three or more charges on a consistent weekly, monthly,
  quarterly, or yearly cadence, and store cadence, average, last charge, next date.
- /subscriptions is home: one row per recurring merchant with amount, cadence,
  next charge, annual cost, and a status of active, price hiked, or dormant. Price
  hiked means the latest charge is over 10 percent above the previous one and it
  sorts to the top, because that row is what pays for this build.
- Three more screens and no others. /transactions, a searchable table where editing
  a category also saves a merchant-to-category rule for the next import. /budgets,
  this month per category against a number I set, total turning red when I am over.
  /networth, monthly balance snapshots per account as a stacked area chart, written
  by the same nightly job.
- Cancelling is a checklist, not a robot: flagging a subscription opens a note with
  the cancellation URL and support email from a cancel-links.json I keep, and the row
  stays flagged until one full cadence passes with no charge, then it self-confirms.
- A Monday morning digest over Resend: new recurring charges found, price hikes, and
  everything charging in the next seven days. Key in .env.
- One SQLite file, no accounts, no telemetry, nothing leaves the machine except the
  Plaid and Resend calls. Out of scope: bill negotiation and cancelling on my behalf,
  both of which are human work, plus credit monitoring, holdings, and mobile apps.
- README: how to get Plaid sandbox keys and move an Item to production, and that
  production is self-serve but metered per linked Item, so keep the bank count small.
